record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Describe all lattice orders on the free soluble ℓ-group on a finite number n (> 1) of generators.

evidence.quote: 1.3. Describe all lattice orders on the free soluble ℓ-group on a finite number n (> 1) of generators.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is a group G equipped with a partial order ≤ that is a lattice and is invariant under left and right multiplication: for all a,b,x,y ∈ G, a ≤ b implies xay ≤ xby. Morphisms of ℓ-groups are group homomorphisms that also preserve the lattice operations ∧ and ∨. The variety of ℓ-groups thus has free objects: for a set X, the free ℓ-group on X is the ℓ-group F(X) together with a map X → F(X) such that any map from X into an ℓ-group extends uniquely to an ℓ-group homomorphism from F(X). An ℓ-group G is soluble (solvable) if its underlying group is soluble, and the variety of soluble ℓ-groups (of a fixed derived length, or all soluble ℓ-groups) has free objects in the corresponding sense; denote by S_n the free soluble ℓ-group on n generators.

By a "lattice order" on a group H one means a translation-invariant lattice order on H making it an ℓ-group. Two lattice orders are considered the same if they coincide as partial orders (equivalently, have the same positive cone).

Problem. Fix an integer n > 1. Describe explicitly all lattice orders on the free soluble ℓ-group S_n on n generators; that is, classify all positive cones P ⊆ S_n that endow the underlying group of S_n with the structure of a lattice-ordered group.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing all lattice orders on the free soluble ℓ-group on n > 1 generators is listed among unsolved problems in ordered/orderable groups and does not appear to have been resolved. Recent literature on free ℓ-groups and orderings on free groups discusses related questions (e.g., decidability of the word problem, right-orderings on free groups by Clay–Smith) but does not provide a classification of lattice orders on free soluble ℓ-groups.
